procedural_matters: GER 3442 was represented by Amelia Kutz (helm).
GBR 3491 was represented by Basil Sanderson Wood (crew).
The panel of the International Jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
facts: The conditions during the time of the incident were 17 kts of wind and light chop.
When entering the zone of mark 2p for the last time, GER 3442 and GBR 3491 were sailing on port tack towards the mark, with GER 3442 overlapped approximately 8 boat lengths to windward of GBR 3491.
GER 3442 was sailing nearly on running course and GBR 3491 was sailing on higher course.
When GER 3442 was at the mark, she was close to it and the lateral distance between the hulls was about 1 m.
GBR 3491 heeled the boat to windward and the top of her mast went through the main sail of GER 3442, resulting in a 20 cm tear in the upper part of the main sail of GER 3442.
GER 3442's coach taped the sail between races 2 and 3.
GER 3442 stated that the feel of the sail was ''weird'' in race 3, however she made no claim that her score was made significantly worse.
GER 3442 finished race 1 in 21st place, race 2 in 26th place and race 3 in 26th place.
conclusions: GBR 3491 outside overlapped at the zone failed to give GER 3442 mark-room, and broke RRS 18.2(a)(1).
GBR 3491 did not avoid contact with GER 3442 even though it was reasonably possible, and broke RRS 14(a).
GER 3442 to windward failed to keep clear of GBR 3491 to leeward, and broke RRS 11.
Since GER 3442 broke RRS 11 while she was sailing within the mark-room to which she was entitled, she is exonerated under RRS 43.1(b) for this breach.

It was not reasonably possible for GER 3442 the boat sailing within the mark-room to which she was entitled to avoid contact with GBR 3491 when it became clear that GBR 3491 was not giving mark-room. GER 3442 did not break RRS 14(a).
GER 3442 ’s place in race 3 was not made significantly worse. Therefore, the requirements for redress in RRS 61.4(b) are not met.
decision: GBR is DSQ in race 2. Redress not given
